meta.description: Numeric thresholds and constraints for lunar south-pole landing-site and landing-window selection (lighting, Earth visibility, slope, latitude, surface-stay length, orbit periods, eclipse limits, rover rules, ISRU criteria, study screening values).
meta.coordinate_convention: Decimal degrees; latitude south negative; longitude east-positive (-180..180 and 0..360 where coordinates appear).
notes: Values copied from research notes of 2026-11-14; not independently validated.

status vocabulary: 'formal requirement' (stated NASA/mission requirement; notes label REQ), 'mission choice' (mission-specific design choice or screening value; CHOICE), 'rule of thumb' (descriptive statement; RULE), 'study criterion' (threshold used in a published non-NASA or research study), 'measured/analysis result', 'superseded' (belonged to a plan no longer current). 'superseded' may be combined with another status.

IMPORTANT: the NRHO-based Artemis III design (6.5-day stay, one descent per NRHO revolution, Starship HLS) was superseded in 2026. Artemis III is now a 2027 LEO test; the first landing is Artemis IV (2028) via low lunar orbit (Starship) or an elliptical polar orbit (Blue Moon MK2). NASA has published no window/availability numbers for the new architecture; NRHO-era numbers are legacy.
Values taken from NTRS 20230005904 (PlatteCity_Artemis.pdf) were decoded from an obfuscated PDF text layer and should be checked visually; the same constraints also appear in NTRS 20250009323.

No NASA source gives a numeric minimum/maximum Sun elevation at touchdown, a Sun-azimuth-vs-approach limit, a minimum Earth elevation (mask angle) for DTE, or pad-separation / distance-to-PSR thresholds for a base.
value is a number where the source gives a single number, otherwise a string.
